title: Codekick
user: Two to four friends who want an immediate browser football match through a room code, on laptop keyboard or touch, without downloads or an account.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The Show HN launch explicitly offers multiplayer browser football with server-authoritative physics; a commenter says they plan to play it after work, evidence of ready-to-try demand.
The fetched official page describes 0-0.io as real-time browser football with no download and no signup.

recurrence: The recent launch and immediate player response validate drop-in browser football; this is a competitive format where queues, control complexity, and long matches remain the likely friction.
current_workaround: Download a large football game, join a public .io queue, or abandon play when both friends cannot matchmake together.
incumbents_and_gap: 0-0.io and other .io sports games validate instant browser sports, but public queues and physics-heavy controls are not ideal for two friends arriving from a shared link. A deliberately small code-room duel is underserved.
smallest_useful_product: A 2v2, four-minute arcade football match: host shares a room code, each player has move/pass/shot, and possession grants a visible two-second combo window. Each match differs through one symmetric stadium rule (wind, bounce, goal shape). Non-goals: leagues, player packs, realistic simulation, public matchmaking, or licensed teams.
success_measure: 75% of created rooms get two players connected in under a minute, and at least half of finished matches include a rematch.
monetization: free — the first requirement is a sendable two-friend game; cosmetic stadiums can be a one-time purchase later.
constraints: Server-authoritative state with interpolation; compensate for latency but do not promise esports fairness; generic teams and original art only; support keyboard and touch.
why_distinct: It is a short private-room social sport, not an attempt to clone FIFA or build an .io matchmaking economy.
